description: A rename (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT -> DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) migrated http.py but left client.py and server.py — both changed by the PR — importing the old name: ImportError at import time. TWO findings, one per stale importer, sharing a `group`: this is the multi-finding command ADR-0013 exists for, and the first plan scenario to exercise it. The commanded fix spans files, so ADR-0009's atomicity rule requires the stacked-PR shape: all-patch fix steps plus push_branch then open_pr. Per-file suggestions could be half-applied, leaving the branch broken in a way neither reviewer nor contributor intended — and a MULTI-FILE all-suggest plan still VERIFIES (containment has no cross-step check and cardinality bounds suggestions per file, not per plan) — so this grader is still the only automated thing standing between the model and the executor here.
commanded_note: The scenario was UNSATISFIABLE before ADR-0013 and failed 0/3 on measurement, which was the fixture and not the model: one finding was commanded, anchored to constants.py, while the grader below requires the fix to touch client.py and server.py — and check_commanded_scope requires the fix to touch every COMMANDED path. No plan could satisfy both, so the model's alias-in-constants.py answer was the only shape that could pass the gate, and it was graded wrong. A one-anchor finding cannot scope a multi-file fix (ADR-0009's addendum C), which is exactly what the set-valued command fixes: commanding BOTH importers makes the coordinated fix expressible AND gives stacked delivery its first reachable trigger in an eval. Do not collapse this back to one ordinal.
shape_note: fix_paths_must_include, not must_equal: both stale importers must be fixed, and constants.py is left to the model's judgment (reverting the rename is also coherent — but http.py already uses the new name, so must_not_include pins that the fix moves forward, not back). The invariant graded is kinds-uniform + write-chain-iff-patch; how the model splits patches across the two files is not pinned.
